partner_result_applied.result: Rank-two averaged endpoint and independent-third-square closure; used as the exact coupling debt that the new theorem pays on a nonindependent 3x2 cross-minor branch.

proved_results: For disjoint original-coordinate sets I,K with |I|=3, |K|=2 and rank M=A[I,K]=2, let nu span ker(M^T), a=nu^T A[I,I]nu, Delta=sqrt(det(M^T M)). If a!=0 then Q has a bounded continuous density.

The proof retains all outside couplings: two K-coordinates are removed by 2D Plancherel after rotating only the three integration coordinates I; the transverse null direction is controlled by the prior scalar L3 quadratic gate and a weighted dt/t estimate.
Product provenance is used in the exact slice estimate m(u)<=sqrt(3); arbitrary bounded joint replacement is not made.
unresolved_implication: AGGREGATED-RANK2-TRANSVERSE-GATE: replace reciprocal payment for one fixed 3x2 cross minor by a dimension-free many-column/bank anti-concentration estimate under the three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis, while retaining transverse curvature.
next_step: Develop a many-column version of the 2D Plancherel randomizer in which the density of the rank-two linear bank is paid by aggregate coefficient energy rather than one determinant; test it first on A_m=[1] direct_sum J_m/m direct_sum (-J_m/m).
